source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Older adults are more susceptible to dizziness, sedation, and hypotension from diphenhydramine, so the prescription warrants caution and safety assessment.","B":"Older adults usually develop less sedation and dizziness from diphenhydramine than younger adults, so age alone reduces concern about adverse effects.","C":"Diphenhydramine improves alertness in older adults despite its antihistamine effects, so it is preferred when allergy treatment must avoid drowsiness.","D":"Diphenhydramine has no age-related precautions for dizziness or blood pressure effects, so routine geriatric medication review is unnecessary when this drug is prescribed."}}
source_row.rationale: Diphenhydramine labeling specifically notes that older adults are more likely to experience dizziness, sedation, and hypotension. Option A accurately identifies those age-related safety concerns. Option B incorrectly claims reduced susceptibility. Option C contradicts diphenhydramine's sedating effect. Option D incorrectly denies the geriatric precautions described in the label.
